What slows manufacturing teams down

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

  • Enquiries scattered across marketplaces and inboxes

    IndiaMART and TradeIndia leads, website forms, trade-fair cards and phone calls land in different places. Coordinators copy them by hand, duplicates reach two reps, and enquiries that arrive late in the evening or during a trade fair wait while competitors reply.

  • Quotes that depend on a few people

    Estimators rebuild costing sheets for every RFQ, recall past prices from memory and chase purchase for current material rates. When they are on the shop floor or traveling, quotes wait and the assumptions behind a price go unrecorded.

  • Dealer orders that live outside the ERP

    Orders arrive as WhatsApp texts, photos of handwritten lists and calls that the order desk re-types into Tally or the ERP. Stock, schemes and credit are checked by phone afterwards, and errors surface at dispatch or in the next dealer complaint.

  • Credit and collections on spreadsheets

    Credit limits and overdue balances sit with accounts while reps keep booking orders. Reminders depend on who has time, and disputes about schemes, credit notes or short supply appear only when a payment is already late.

  • Plant data that arrives late and disagrees

    Shift output, downtime and rejections come from ERP entries, Excel sheets and photos of logbooks. Morning meetings debate the numbers instead of acting on them, and maintenance and quality follow-ups slip between shifts.

  • Compliance that touches every workflow

    E-invoices, e-way bills, BIS licenses, GMP records, messaging consent and personal data rules all shape how orders, dispatches and plant records may be automated. A shortcut in one workflow can create risk in another.

Enquiry-to-quote desk for B2B manufacturers

One connected workflow from the moment an RFQ arrives on IndiaMART, the website or email to an approved quote and a confirmed sales order. AI structures enquiries and specifications and flags what it cannot read with confidence, the costing draft is built from your own item master and rates, and your estimator and commercial team approve every price, discount and order before anything reaches the buyer or the ERP.

What changes

  • Fewer enquiries lost between marketplaces, inboxes and the CRM
  • Faster, more consistent first responses and quote turnaround
  • Quotes built on current rates with recorded assumptions and approvals
  • Clear win and loss reasons by product, source and region
  1. 1

    Capture every enquiry in one queue

    Leads from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, other marketplaces, website forms and the RFQ inbox flow into the CRM, matched against existing accounts and open enquiries so no buyer gets two reps or none.

    nn8nZCZoho CRM
  2. 2

    Read, qualify and route

    An AI model extracts product, grade or specification, quantity, location and timeline from the message and attachments, lists missing details as questions for the first call, and routes the enquiry to the right owner with a response deadline.

    OOpenAInn8nSSlack
  3. 3

    Build the costing draft

    Each line is matched to the item master, released drawing revisions and past quotes, then costed with the current material, conversion, tooling and freight rates that purchase and costing maintain.

    PPythonSSupabase
  4. 4

    Estimator reviews and approves

    The estimator corrects the draft in a review screen, records assumptions and deviations from the buyer's specification, and approves it. Discounts outside the agreed matrix go to the sales head.

    RRetoolSSlack
  5. 5

    Send, follow up and learn

    The approved quote goes out as a PDF from the rep's address, follow-ups are scheduled in the CRM, and win or loss reasons are captured by product, source and region.

    RResendZCZoho CRM
  6. 6

    Turn the PO into a sales order

    When the buyer's PO arrives, it is compared with the approved quote for price, quantity, delivery and terms, checked against the credit position, and staged as a draft sales order for the commercial manager to release in the ERP.

    ACAnthropic Claudenn8n

  7. People decide

    The estimator approves every technical interpretation and price before a quote is sent, the sales head approves discounts outside the agreed matrix, and the commercial manager resolves PO-to-quote mismatches and releases the sales order in the ERP. AI drafts and checks; people decide.

A clear delivery rhythm

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 1

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We map how enquiries, orders, production data, quality records and dispatch actually flow today, sit with the order desk, estimators and plant teams, and pick the workflows where automation helps most. We baseline the KPIs from existing ERP and CRM data and identify GST, GxP and data protection boundaries early.

  2. 2

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design each workflow with its triggers, data fields, decision rules, approval points and failure paths, plus the WhatsApp templates and review screens people will use. For regulated sites we agree with QA where each automation sits relative to validated systems and what change control it needs.

  3. 3

    2–6 weeks

    Build

    We build integrations, workflows, review screens and dashboards in a test environment, using sample or anonymized data where possible, with logging, alerts and role-based access from the start. Each workflow is demonstrated to its owners as it takes shape.

  4. 4

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    Owners test each workflow against real scenarios, including credit holds, partial dispatches, e-way bill extensions and low-confidence AI extractions. We launch to a pilot group first, run alongside the existing process for a short period, and train the people who approve work and handle exceptions.

  5. 5

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    We monitor runs, failures and AI accuracy, review KPIs with the owners each month, tune rules and prompts, and add the next workflows from the backlog. Every change follows the same design, test and approval route as the original build.

First pilot: Enquiry-to-quote pilot for one product family

A four to six week pilot that connects IndiaMART, website forms and the RFQ inbox for one product family, routes qualified enquiries to their owners and gives the estimator a costing draft to approve. Pharma plants can instead pilot a read-only batch release board for one product line, timed around change control. We compare first-response and quote turnaround with the baseline and decide together whether to extend.

  • Enquiry capture from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, website forms and one RFQ mailbox
  • Extraction, deduplication and routing rules for one product family and region
  • Costing draft and estimator review screen for repeat items that already have cost data
  • Response-time and quote-turnaround dashboard compared with the baseline
  • Training for sales coordinators and estimators, followed by a go or no-go review

Know whether it is working

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Enquiry first-response time
Median time from an enquiry arriving in any channel to the first meaningful human response, measured in business hours.
Quote turnaround time
Median time from an enquiry being marked qualified to the approved quote being sent, by product family.
Quote-to-order conversion
Share of quotes sent in a period that become purchase orders, tracked by product, source and region.
On-time-in-full dispatch
Share of order lines dispatched complete by the date promised to the customer or dealer.
